newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain says floods cause extensive crop damage.
newsitem.headline: Spain says floods cause extensive crop damage.

text.p: Spain's agriculture minister said on Monday she feared floods in southern Spain had caused extensive crop damage and would not rule out declaring the area a disaster zone.

The rains had eased by Monday but floods persisted after a week of heavy downpour in the Andalusia region burst river banks and inundated roads, fields and villages, forcing thousands to evacuate their homes.

"We have seen the effects on the agricultural sector, which will be fully studied once the water subsides, but evidently it is of great magnitude and tens of thousands of hectares have been affected," Agriculture Minister Loyola de Palacio told a press conference.

Andalusian Farmers' Union UAGA-COAG said the rains had caused around 75 billion pesetas ($573 million) of crop damage with strawberries, olives, potatoes, citric fruits, winter grains and beets the worst hit.
After surveying the worst hit regions by helicopter, de Palacio said the government would work swiftly to evaluate the exact damage and then take the appropriate measures.

"We will have to see what types of measures are most appropriate, perhaps some type of extraordinary funding or another measure agreed with Andalusia's regional government," she said, without ruling out the possibility of declaring the area a disaster zone.
De Palacio said in the Huelva province, fruits and vegetables appeared to be badly damaged while the effects on winter cereals had been more varied.
"Citrus fruits appear very badly affected and olive groves will also have suffered severe damage with a great part of the harvest not yet gathered," she said.
UAGA-COAG estimated that in the Cordoba province around 60 percent of the olive crops had been damaged, representing economic losses of between 15 and 20 percent.
